exitCode.description: Only when T3 reports one or the output says "Exit code N"; T3's Claude adapter sets none itself.

envName.description: secret with an env: sink: the variable it writes, when not the one its key names (`secretEnvName`).

evidence.description: What closed or reopened it: "fingerprint ab12cd34", a gated run's exit code and output tail, a failed verify.

fingerprint.description: secret: set when the node has written the sink.

gated.description: Required for approve; immutable once the ask exists.

number.description: Fixed within its batch; never renumbered.

permission.description: approve: the session prompt it answers, instead of `gated`.

proceededOnRec.description: The lead carried on with the recommendation; the answer confirms or overrides it.

projectRef.description: Absent only on an `intake.route.*` ask: the human picks the project by answering it.

verify.description: do: the check the hub runs once the human ticks it done; a failure reopens the ask with the evidence.

raw.description: The reply text it was parsed from.

AskKind.description:
decide: a product call. do: hand steps for the human, optionally re-checked by `verify`. secret: a value the
desktop app seals to the sink's node. approve: a stored command the node runs after a human approves it.

asks.description: The asks in those batches, by batch then number.

Attention.description:
Whether an event needs the human now, set by the hub when it emits the event. "loud": notify, but hold it through
quiet hours; "urgent": notify even during quiet hours (money and irreversible). Absent: the inbox and the digest
are enough.

coalesceSec.description: At most one notification per this many seconds; what arrives meanwhile is folded into the next.

quiet.description: Only "urgent" events notify inside these; empty when quiet hours are off. Ask again after the last one ends.

baseline.description: Research: what the candidate is compared against, and how both are measured.

decisionRule.description: Research: frozen with the brief, so the verdict can't move the goalposts.

doneWhen.description: At least one; frozen with the brief.

metric.description: Research: the one number the judge reports for baseline and candidate, e.g. "p50 cold start in ms".

lastError.description: The refusal fix, conflicting paths, or failing check names.

mergedSha.description: The squash commit on the base; set on merge.

position.description: 0-based index into its train's queue; absent when not queued.

taskId.description: The write task that opened it; absent when the lead enqueued a PR no task wrote.

tier.description: From the workstream's brief; may be raised, never lowered.

ChangeReview.description: One review verdict, valid for exactly this patch. A clean rebase that keeps the patch id keeps it valid.

CheckOutcome.description: `error` (the check could not run) counts as not passing.

evidence.description: Output tail, HTTP status and body excerpt, verdict summary, or the fix when `error`.

exitCode.description: Only for `cmd` checks, which the node runs.

CommitSha.description: Full lowercase hex commit SHA, 40 or 64 characters

askId.description: The ask this answers, when it came from one.

by.description: Who recorded it: the agent key name, "lead:<machineId>/<projectId>" or "human:<device>".

supersedes.description: The earlier active decision on the same key and scope that this one replaced.

DecisionRule.description:
Applied to the improvement: candidate − baseline, negated when lower is better. GO when it is at least
`goAtLeast`, STOP when it is below `stopBelow`, INCONCLUSIVE in between.

DecisionSource.description: Filled by the hub from the caller: a human device, an agent key, or a lead-side call.

decisions.description: Best match first; active decisions only.

fix.description: Absent when there is nothing to do.

DoctorFix.description: `auto`: doctor_fix runs it. `manual`: a person runs `command` (where the label says).

check.description: The check, run again after the fix.

ran.description: What the fix did, in plain words.

checks.description: Hub checks first, then each machine's, in a fixed order.

DoctorStatus.description: `unknown`: the hub could not look (machine offline, nothing to read).

Eta.description: The brief's raw estimate corrected by the tier's measured actual/raw ratio.

ratio.description: Median actual/raw over the tier's last 20 done workstreams; the 5.0 prior below 5 samples.

cursor.description: Absent means start at the current end.

attention.description: Latest failed, waiting and usage-limited events, and PRs the merge train sent back to their authors.

slots.description: Absent until the hub runs the slot board (M5).

GatedRunSpec.description: Stored with the approve ask and never changed: the human approves exactly these bytes.

data.description: At most 2 KB of JSON; the hub trims before emitting.

oneOf.description: T3 no longer has the project: the hub dropped it from its cache, and its open workstreams stop. `data.title`.
Needs approval or user input.
No progress past the stall threshold; the hub interrupts and nudges once.
A wake missed while the hub was down, with catchUp "skip".
A queued write to an offline machine was delivered when it came back.
A queued write outlived its TTL and was dropped.
A webhook subscription has been failing for over an hour.
The brief was frozen; `data.briefHash`.
An ask was answered from the decision log and never reached a batch.
The human digest is ready; no project content, since every key sees it. Read it with digest_get. `data.at`.
`data.queuedReason`.
A write task's diff touched files outside its leased areas; `data.paths`.
A lease held for over 4 h; flagged once, never released by the hub. `data.taskId`, `data.area`.
A claim had a failing check; the workstream stays verifying. `data.claimId`, `data.workstreamId`.
Every done-when check passed. `data.workstreamId`.
`data.taskId`, `data.prHeadSha`, `data.blocking`.
`data.incidentId`, `data.class`.
`data.changeId`, `data.repo`, `data.prNumber`.
Its tier's reviews are satisfied for the current patch id. `data.changeId`.
The rebase conflicted; `data.changeId`, `data.paths`.
`data.changeId`, `data.checks` (failing check names), `data.logUrl`.
`data.changeId`, `data.repo`, `data.prNumber`, `data.mergedSha`.
`data.repo`, `data.reason`.
`data.repo`.
Refused at enqueue; `data.prUrl`, `data.fix`.
Where an intent went; `data.workstreamId` or `data.askId`, `data.template`, `data.reason`, `data.playbook`.
A research workstream's computed verdict; `data.workstreamId`, `data.outcome`, `data.metricValues`.
M4: a machine's login hit the same limit on several threads, or its proxy has no account; dispatch there pauses.
M4: parked threads were sent "continue" at their reset or on usage_resume; `data.breakerCleared`.
M8: the node wrote a secret's sink. `data.askId`, `data.fingerprint`, `data.by` (the human who submitted it).
M8: the node ran an approved command. `data.askId`, `data.exitCode`, `data.timedOut`, `data.by` (the approver).
M11: doctor checks changed status; `data.changes` lists `{ id, from, to }` (from absent on the first run).
M12: a retro run ended; `data.run`, `data.trigger`, `data.advise`, `data.proposals`, `data.dropped`, `data.usage` (orchestrator runs).
M12: a playbook file changed under a retro proposal; `data.proposalId`, `data.playbook`, `data.ref`, `data.previousRef`, `data.kind`, `data.baseline`, `data.dueAt`.
M12: a wording change missed its metric or regressed a guarded one and was rolled back; `data.proposalId`, `data.reason`.
M12: a wording change met its metric; `data.proposalId`, `data.measured`.
A device redeemed a pairing code from `fleetd pair` and got a human key; `data.keyId`, `data.deviceName`.

number.description: The batch item number; absent for "pref:" and "forget".

source.description: The written decision's source and by, filled by the hub from the caller (human device or agent key).

raw.description: Terse reply such as "1 go 2 nvm 3 recs fine"; a leading "#B<n>" picks the batch.

InboxReplyOutcome.description: answered: a Decision was written. later: moved to the next batch. retired: "forget Dn". pref: "pref:" recorded.

hint.description: How to fix an unparseable reply.

Incident.description: Recorded by the hub, never by an agent.

evidence.description: Plain-language lines: claim ids with their failing checks, ratios, SHAs.

IncidentClass.description:
`policy_bypass`: a PR on a watched repo was merged by something other than the train. M12: `re_ask`, a human was
asked about a key that already had an active Decision; `override`, a human replaced a lead's Decision with another
value; `playbook_reverted`, a retro wording change missed its metric and was rolled back.

windowDays.description: M12: the span `counts` covers, ending now.

counts.description:
M12: incidents per class since `counts_since`, under the same filters; classes with none are left out. Most
first.

IntakeEcho.description: Where an intent went and why, whether the router, a prefix, `@<project>` or the caller decided it.

machineId.description: With projectId, or neither: then the router picks the project unless the text starts with `@<project>`.

template.description: Skips the router for the template, like a `fix:` or `research:` prefix.

askId.description: The router could not place the intent: the human picks the project by answering this ask.

idle.description: The project's finish-all workstream went (or stayed) idle: nothing left with a value source.

spawnable.description: Items with a value source that no open child serves yet.

text.description: The ranked list, one item per line.

parked.description: M4: the lead thread hit a usage limit; derived from the usage layer when read.

threadId.description: The current lead thread on the project's machine; earlier ones stay in T3 as history.

model.description:
Saved as the project's lead model and effort for this and later (re)starts; absent keeps the saved or hub
default.

parked.description: M4: the lead thread hit a usage limit; derived from the usage layer when read.

threadId.description: The current lead thread on the project's machine; earlier ones stay in T3 as history.

LoginKind.description: Read from the T3 provider instance status and its env var names, never from credentials.

boxPubKey.description:
M8: the node's X25519 key from its hello; clients seal this machine's secrets to it. Absent: it takes no
secrets.

degradedReason.description: Plain language, set while status is "degraded".

t3.description: Null until the node has reported a reachable T3.

MetricValues.description: The judge's reported numbers for the brief's metric.

OrchestratorRun.description: A `claude -p` one-shot the hub ran for itself, counted as orchestrator usage.

PatchId.description: Full lowercase hex patch id, 40 or 64 characters

PlaybookName.description: The prefixes `bug:`/`fix:`, `research:` and `finish:` pick bugfix, research and finish-all.

PlaybookRef.description: <playbook name>@<full lowercase hex git blob SHA>

ProbeCounter.description: Direct usage or reset-credit calls seen in the machine's T3 trace file. Must be 0.

source.description: The trace directory read, when observable.

created.description: False when the directory was already a project (it is renamed when a title is given).

ProjectOutcome.description: The one-call project outcome, returned as-is by project_get.

taskCounts.description: Absent until the project has a task.

threads.description: Newest activity first. Task threads are left out; they show under `tasks`.

trains.description: The merge trains of the project's repos; absent until one of its PRs was enqueued.

truncated.description: True when `threads`, `workstreams` or `tasks` was trimmed to its limit.

workstreams.description: Open workstreams (not done, stopped or failed), newest first.

Receipts.description: Counted by the hub from the task's T3 items, never from its prose.

ResearchOutcome.description: STOP is a success: the question was answered.

ResearchVerdict.description: Computed by the hub, never reported by an agent; `outcome` always follows from `rule` and `metricValues`.

windowDays.description: Measured over this many days after the change, against the same span before it.

RetroMetricClass.description:
The fixed metric list, defined in code: incident counts per class, and agent-minutes per done workstream. A
proposal names one; the retro cannot add or change them.

baseline.description: The window before it applied; `measured` is the window after.

claimedKind.description: What the model said it was.

dueAt.description: When a wording change's window ends and its metric is computed.

fields.description: Frontmatter fields the diff changes, plus "body".

kind.description: Decided by the hub from the fields the diff touches.

ref.description: The version it applied and the one it replaced.

run.description: The retro run that proposed it.

RetroProposalState.description:
suggested: advise-only, nothing applies. pending: a gate change waiting for the weekly Ask; asked: in it.
measuring: a wording change applied, its window running; then kept or reverted. applied: a gate change a person
approved. rejected: a person said no. stale: the playbook changed under it, so its diff no longer applies.

apply.description: The global Decision policy.retro.apply is true: wording changes apply on their own and gate changes are asked.

advise.description: Nothing it proposed applies: `--advise`, or `policy.retro.apply` is not true.

incidents.description: Incidents in the window it was given.

usage.description: Absent when there was nothing to look at and no turn ran.

RetroRunDropped.description: A change the hub refused, with why.

advise.description: Propose only, even when policy.retro.apply is true.

RetroSnapshot.description:
A metric's values over one window; agent-minutes is null when no workstream finished in it. Its keys are
snake_case on the wire.

SecretFingerprint.description: 8 lowercase hex characters: the sha256 prefix of the plaintext

sealed.description: Sealed in the desktop app to the sink machine's `box_pub_key` (see Machine).

reservedBand.description: Slots of the cap only lead turns may take.

expect.description: What the human should see when the step worked.

Subscription.description: A webhook push target. Its signing secret is shown once by subscription_set and never returned again.

createdBy.description: keyId of the agent key that created it.

failingSince.description: When deliveries started failing; absent while healthy.

secret.description: The webhook signing secret. Shown only here; store it now.

parked.description: M4: its thread hit a usage limit; the task is idle until fleetd sends "continue" at `resumeAt`.

pr.description: The PR a review task reviews. Required at spawn for review; absent on hub-spawned judge tasks and older rows.

queuedReason.description: Why it is queued, e.g. "lease: docs held by T1" or "slots: 40/40 in use".

serves.description: Required at spawn for write tasks; optional here for tasks stored before M6.

TaskCounts.description: A project's tasks by state, all time.

TaskKind.description: Only write tasks get a worktree and leases.

claimsUnverified.description: The tail claims success ("tests pass", "fixed", ...) while `receipts.commands` is 0. Absent before M6.

receipts.description: Absent on results stored before M6.

tail.description: The latest assistant message, trimmed to its last 2000 characters.

message.description: Deny only: what claude is told instead of running the tool.

requestId.description: The prompt answered, from the thread.waiting event; absent means the one open now.

askId.description: The tool_permission ask this answer closed, if one was open.

queued.description: True when the machine is offline and the message waits in the hub's queue.

queuedUntil.description: When a queued message expires undelivered.

effort.description: As reported by T3; not narrowed to Effort because T3 may report other levels.

headline.description: First line of the latest visible assistant text.

ToolPermission.description:
An approve ask raised by a session's tool permission prompt (`tool_permission`) instead of a gated command: answering
it answers the prompt on the project's node. Its machine is the ask's project's.

summary.description: The command, the path, or the tool's own description.

head.description: The Change being rebased, checked or merged now.

UsageBreaker.description: Open: no new turns start on the machine's login until `until` or usage_resume.

message.description: The plain notice, as the usage.breaker event said it.

until.description: Absent while open means until usage_resume.

UsageClass.description:
What stopped a turn. `usage_limit`: the plan's usage limit or a proxy cooldown, with a reset. `rate_limit`: a 429.
`pool_exhausted`: the user's proxy has no account for the model; it waits for usage_resume.

UsageParked.description: A task or lead whose thread hit a limit; fleetd sends it one "continue" at `resume_at`.

resumeAt.description: Absent for pool_exhausted: it resumes on usage_resume.

lastEvents.description: The latest thread.usage_limited, usage.breaker and usage.resumed events for the machine, oldest first.

catchUp.description: What to do with a firing missed while the hub was down.

createdBy.description: keyId of the agent key that set it.

nextRunAt.description: Absent once the wake is done or cancelled.

WakeCron.description: Standard 5-field cron; the hub parses it.

estimateActual.description: Hub-filled, outside the frozen brief. Set when it starts running with a raw estimate.

outcome.description: Research workstreams, once the verdict is computed; set together with `verdict`. A STOP is done, not failed.

parent.description: M9 finish-all: the finish-all workstream that spawned this one, and the value source it was spawned for.

playbook.description: Pinned at creation; the brief freeze validates against this version. Absent on workstreams from before M9.

actualMinutes.description: Wall-clock minutes from running to done; set on done.

ratioAtStart.description: The tier's calibration ratio when it started running.

eta.description: Absent without a raw estimate in the brief.

by.description: Who submitted it: an agent keyId, "human" or "lead:<machineId>/<projectId>".

parent.description: The project's open finish-all workstream it is a child of.
